description: Exception caught and swallowed: returned False/None after error logging without re-raising, or exception caught but neither logged nor re-raised.
why_forbidden: Produces invisible data loss. An OCR pass that silently fails leaves the user with empty output and no signal to retry. The cost of silence is unbounded; the cost of a crash is a restart.
detection_test: Does any except block (a) log the exception but return a falsy value instead of re-raising, (b) catch and pass without logging, or (c) catch and continue processing on bad state? If yes: silent failure.
required_shape: Log with exc_info=True, call flush_loggers(), then raise. No return-False-after-error path. No catch-and-continue.

description: Fallback instantiation in an expression: `x or SomeClass()`, `x if condition else SomeClass()`, `dict.get(key, SomeClass())`, `getattr(obj, attr, SomeClass())`. Creates a silent default when the real dependency is absent.
why_forbidden: Masks misconfiguration. A missing Google Cloud client that falls back to a default instance silently produces no OCR output. The correct shape is: validate at startup, crash if absent.
detection_test: Does any expression construct a class instance as the fallback branch of `or`, ternary, `.get()`, or `getattr()`? If yes: dodgy fallback.
required_shape: Validate presence of dependencies at startup (in __init__ or module load). Raise immediately if absent. No fallback construction expressions.

description: Business logic, file I/O, data transformation, or algorithmic work placed in ui/ methods. UI layer becomes a second processing engine alongside workers/.
why_forbidden: Untestable without a running Qt application. Duplicates logic that belongs in workers or pipeline stages. Violates the thin-delegation contract of §4. Early-stage liquefaction.
detection_test: Does any method in ui/ do file reading/writing, OCR result parsing, Greek text transformation, PDF manipulation, or algorithmic work beyond simple display delegation? If yes: UI second engine.
required_shape: UI methods: receive user gesture, delegate to worker or utility, update display state, show user-facing error. Nothing else. Max ~15 lines.

description: Code in processing/, pipeline/, or utils/ imports from ui/ or workers/. Or ui/ imports directly from pipeline/ or processing/ bypassing workers/.
why_forbidden: Couples the OCR engine to Qt. Makes the engine untestable without a display. Creates circular dependency risk. Violates the one-way dependency contract of §5.
detection_test: Does any file under processing/, pipeline/, or utils/ contain an import from ui/ or workers/? Does any ui/ file import directly from pipeline/ or processing/ instead of routing through workers/? If yes: boundary violation.
required_shape: ui/ → workers/ → pipeline/ → processing/ → utils/ → models/. One-way only. Workers are the sole bridge between UI and backend.

description: Mock, MagicMock, AsyncMock, @patch, or patch() used in any test or verification file.
why_forbidden: A test that mocks the Google Document AI client does not test OCR. A test that mocks the PDF renderer does not test PDF handling. Mocks verify the mock, not the system. PhilOcr's correctness bar is the accuracy of output Greek text — only a real round-trip can verify that.
detection_test: Does any test_*.py or verif_*.py file import or use Mock, MagicMock, AsyncMock, patch, or @patch? If yes: mock contamination.
required_shape: Real components, real files, real API calls in all verification code. Use pytest fixtures that construct real objects. Avoid calling external paid APIs in unit test suites — use recordings or skip decorators instead of mocks.

description: A pipeline stage performs work that belongs to another stage. Stage 1 applies masks. Stage 2 calls OCR. Stage 3 normalises text. Stage 4 deskews images. Any of these is contamination.
why_forbidden: Stages are independently testable and independently evolvable only if each has one job. Stage contamination is the primary vector of liquefaction (§8): once boundaries blur, they blur further with each subsequent change.
detection_test: Can you name the single job of this stage in one sentence without 'and also'? Does this stage import from another stage's module? Does it duplicate a transformation already performed by an adjacent stage? If yes to any: contamination.
required_shape: Stage 1: PDF → normalised images only. Stage 2: images → masked images only. Stage 3: images → raw OCR result only. Stage 4: raw OCR result → assembled text only. Cross-stage data flows through typed models/ types only.

description: More than one code path parses, interprets, or transforms the raw Google Document AI JSON/object response. Two interpreters will produce different output for the same input as the DocAI response format evolves.
why_forbidden: Violates single authority (§2). Corpus consistency requires bit-identical interpretation of the same OCR output. Two interpreters that diverge by even one character position will corrupt corpus alignment.
detection_test: Is there more than one function or class that reads fields from a DocAI Document object or response dict to produce structured text? If yes: parallel interpreters.
required_shape: One function/class interprets raw DocAI output. All other code receives the interpreted typed model. If the interpretation logic has grown, consolidate into one place and retire the rest.

description: Google Document AI API called directly without routing through RateLimiter in processing/document_ai.py. Includes: instantiating DocumentProcessorServiceClient elsewhere, calling process_document from pipeline stages directly, or importing google.cloud.documentai outside processing/.
why_forbidden: Google Document AI has a hard rate limit (15 req/min default). A single bypass exhausts the quota for the entire batch, producing 429 errors that look like network failures — invisible to the user and fatal to the batch.
detection_test: Does any file outside processing/ import google.cloud.documentai or hold a DocumentProcessorServiceClient instance? Does any pipeline stage call the OCR API without going through processing/document_ai.py? If yes: rate limiter bypass.
required_shape: All Google Document AI calls route through the single client in processing/document_ai.py which owns the RateLimiter. No other file constructs or holds a client.

description: More than one location in the codebase normalises Unicode polytonic Greek text — NFC/NFD conversion, combining diacritics handling, sigma variants, breathing/accent decomposition.
why_forbidden: Ancient Greek has multiple valid Unicode representations. Two normalisers produce divergent output. The Philofree corpus requires consistent normalisation across all source texts; two normalisers guarantee corpus drift.
detection_test: Is there more than one function or method that applies Unicode normalisation (unicodedata.normalize, NFC, NFD) to Greek character sequences, or that rewrites combining diacritics, sigma variants, or breathing marks? If yes: proliferation.
required_shape: One function normalises Greek text. All stages that need normalised output call that one function. If normalisation logic has accreted across multiple sites, consolidate and retire all but one.

description: A function, class, or module between source and consumer that does not add (a) authority narrowing, (b) invariant enforcement, (c) semantic transformation, (d) genuine reuse across 2+ independent call sites, or (e) boundary error isolation. Includes: single-caller modules, relay functions that forward unchanged, wrapper classes whose methods all delegate.
why_forbidden: Each non-load-bearing hop widens the surface to maintain, obscures the actual owner, and adds naming/parameter cost with zero amortisation. The edit distance between intent and effect grows, and with it the risk of divergence.
detection_test: For each intermediate: does it transform, narrow, enforce, or provide genuine reuse? If none of the five criteria hold: delete and inline. All five must fail to classify as AP-010; passing any one means the intermediate is load-bearing.
required_shape: Direct call from intent to owner. Extract a boundary only when it passes at least one of the five criteria. Single-caller modules retire into their sole caller's file.

description: Runtime code uses a hardcoded default when an environment variable or config key is absent, instead of raising immediately. Includes: `os.getenv('KEY', 'default_value')` for required settings, `config.get('key', SomeDefault())`, silent fallback to a default processor ID or project ID.
why_forbidden: Masked misconfiguration. An OCR processor running against the wrong Google Cloud project silently bills the wrong account. A missing processor ID that falls back to a hardcoded one silently processes against stale configuration.
detection_test: Does any os.getenv() or config.get() call for a *required* setting provide a non-None default? Does any startup path continue if a required environment variable is absent? If yes: config fallback.
required_shape: Required env vars checked at startup with explicit raise (or sys.exit) and a clear error message if absent. No defaults for required settings. os.getenv() without a default for required keys.

description: Class, module, abstraction, or capability added for anticipated future need without a current load-bearing use. Includes: base classes with one subclass, registries with one registered item, plugin systems with one plugin, helper utilities called from one site.
why_forbidden: Speculative infrastructure is tomorrow's rot. It adds maintenance surface and naming cost today in exchange for a hypothetical benefit that may never arrive. The correct move is to add it when the second use case materialises.
detection_test: Does this abstraction have more than one independent caller today? Would removing it require changing more than one call site? If no to either: speculative infrastructure.
required_shape: Abstract when the abstraction already has two use cases. Register when there are two things to register. Provide a base class when there are two subclasses. Until then: concrete and direct.

description: A model object (dataclass, typed dict, list) is returned from an authority method and the caller can mutate its contents, changing the authority's internal state without going through the authority's write path.
why_forbidden: Bypasses single authority (§2). A caller that mutates the returned model has written state without any invariant checking, logging, or validation. This is how 'fixed in one place, broken in another' bugs arise.
detection_test: Does any authority method return a mutable container (list, dict, dataclass without frozen=True) that is part of the authority's internal state? Can a caller modify the returned value and observe the change through a subsequent read? If yes: mutable leakage.
required_shape: Return frozen dataclasses (frozen=True), tuples, or copies of mutable internal state. Never return references to internal mutable containers. If the model must be mutable, expose a dedicated mutation method.

description: Google Cloud service account keys, project IDs, processor IDs, API keys, or any authentication material hardcoded in .py files, committed in env_config.json with real values, or present in any version-controlled file.
why_forbidden: Credentials in source are public. Google Cloud service account keys in source files are one GitHub push away from being harvested. The damage is unbounded: billing fraud, corpus pollution, data exfiltration.
detection_test: Does any .py file contain a string that looks like a Google Cloud project ID, processor ID, or service account JSON key? Are real credentials committed in env_config.json or any YAML/JSON config? If yes: credentials in source.
required_shape: All credentials in ENV.local (gitignored). env_config.json contains only placeholder values or structural defaults. guardian_064_secrets_leak.py enforces this at pre-commit.
